Below is a 12-week program starting 2026-06-01, structured in three phases. It accounts for menstrual cycle and reported flare windows, and removes HIIT, heavy Valsalva, and jumping during all flow and flare days. The plan includes weekly structure, session details with exercises/sets/reps, deloads, core/pelvic-floor-friendly choices, and recovery guidance. Intensity uses RPE 1–10. “Breath count” = exhale on exertion, avoid breath-holding.

Key dates and constraints
- Cycle info: Last period 2026-05-04; average 27 days, 4 flow days. Expected periods in plan: 
  - ~2026-05-31 to 06-03 (overlaps Week 1)
  - ~2026-06-27 to 06-30 (Week 5)
  - ~2026-07-24 to 07-27 (Week 9)
- Flare windows (no HIIT/jumping/valsava): 2026-07-10 to 07-13 (Week 7), 2026-08-04 to 08-07 (Week 10).
- On flow and flare days: prioritize mobility, low-intensity steady cardio, core/pelvic floor care, light strength with higher reps and controlled breathing.

Global weekly template (unless modified below)
- 4 training days + 1 optional light day + 2 rest days.
- Day A: Lower-body strength
- Day B: Upper-body strength + core
- Day C: Conditioning/tempo intervals or circuits (modified to LISS during flow/flare)
- Day D: Full-body strength + mobility
- Optional Day E: Low-intensity steady state (LISS) cardio/mobility (30–40 min)
- Recovery staples each week: 2–3 pelvic-floor breath sessions (5–8 min), 1–2 gentle yoga/mobility sessions (20–30 min), walking on rest days (20–40 min).

Phase overview
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation and symptom-aware base. Submax loads, technique, breathing, core/pelvic floor activation. RPE 5–7.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Progressive strength/Hypertrophy with careful loading. RPE 6–8, one deload/mod week (Week 7 due to flare).
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Consolidate strength, add controlled power (no jumping on restricted days), refine conditioning. RPE 6–8, deload Week 10 (flare).

Warm-up (each session, 8–12 min)
- 2–3 min easy cardio (bike/elliptical/rower walk)
- Mobility: 1–2 sets of 6–8 reps each: cat-cow, 90/90 hip switches, thoracic open books, ankle rocks.
- Activation: glute bridges, dead bugs, band pull-aparts, scap push-ups (1–2 sets of 8–12).
- Breathing: 3–4 cycles of 4-second nasal inhale, 6–8-second pursed-lip exhale on exertion tasks.

Cool-down (5–8 min)
- Easy walk/bike 2–3 min, light stretching (hips, hamstrings, adductors, glutes, T-spine), 2 min diaphragmatic breathing.

Core and pelvic-floor guidelines
- Favor: dead bug, bird dog, side plank, pallof press, tall/half-kneeling anti-rotation, glute bridge march.
- Avoid heavy Valsalva always; especially strict during flow/flare. Cue: exhale through exertion phase.
- If pelvic pressure/pain: reduce load, swap bilateral to unilateral, shorten ROM, or move to relief positions (child’s pose, knees-to-chest, 90-90 breathing).

Nutrition and recovery (general)
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day; distribute across 3–4 meals.
- Carbs: Moderate (3–5 g/kg/day), slightly higher the day before/after heavier lifts; lower during flare as appetite/tolerance guides.
- Fats: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day, emphasize anti-inflammatory sources (olive oil, nuts, fatty fish, flax/chia).
- Hydration: 30–35 ml/kg/day; add 500–750 ml on training days.
- Cycle-aware: During late luteal/flow/flare, favor warm, easy-to-digest foods; consider magnesium (per clinician guidance), omega-3s, ginger/turmeric if tolerated.
- Sleep: 7–9 hours; wind-down routine; short daytime walk for circadian support.

Week 1 (2026-06-01 to 06-07) — Period expected ~05-31 to 06-03

Here’s a concise, coachable anti-inflammatory nutrition plan to layer onto the 12-week program. It aligns with her cycle and flare windows, emphasizes whole-food, omega-3–rich, high-fiber, low–ultra-processed eating, and is practical for a busy client. Adjust portions to meet body size and goals; use the plate method and the macros below as guardrails, not rigid rules.

Daily anchors
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day from mixed sources (fish, poultry, eggs, fermented dairy if tolerated, legumes, tofu/tempeh). Distribute across 3–4 meals, 25–40 g per meal.
- Carbohydrate: 3–5 g/kg/day baseline. Use the plate method to scale with training: more carbs on heavier strength/tempo days, fewer on deload/flare days.
- Fats: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day emphasizing mono- and omega-3 fats.
- Fiber: 25–35 g/day from varied plants. Aim for 30 different plant foods/week (fruits, veg, herbs/spices, whole grains, legumes, nuts/seeds).
- Hydration: 30–35 ml/kg/day plus 500–750 ml on training days. Include electrolytes if sweating heavily or during hot weather.

Anti-inflammatory plate method (each main meal)
- 1/2 plate colorful vegetables and fruit (crucifers, leafy greens, berries, citrus, tomatoes, peppers, onions, mushrooms).
- 1/4 plate protein (fish 2–4x/week; poultry; legumes/tofu/tempeh; eggs; fermented dairy or Greek yogurt if tolerated).
- 1/4 plate smart carbs (steel-cut oats, quinoa, brown/wild rice, buckwheat, barley, potatoes/sweet potatoes, whole-grain sourdough).
- Fats: 1–2 thumbs per meal from extra-virgin olive oil, avocado, nuts, seeds (flax/chia/walnut), olive-based dressings.
- Herbs/spices daily: turmeric + black pepper, ginger, garlic, cinnamon, rosemary, oregano.

Foods to emphasize
- Fish and seafood: Aim for 3 servings/week minimum, 2 being oily fish (salmon, sardines, mackerel, trout).
- Plant proteins: Lentils, chickpeas, black beans, edamame, tofu/tempeh.
- Fermented/probiotic foods: Kefir/yogurt, sauerkraut, kimchi, miso. If dairy is not well tolerated, choose coconut/soy kefir or probiotic foods.
- Polyphenol-rich: Berries, cherries, pomegranate, olive oil, cocoa (85% dark chocolate), green/hibiscus tea, coffee if tolerated.
- Nuts/seeds: Walnuts, almonds, pistachios, pumpkin, chia, flax; grind flax for best absorption.
- Whole grains and resistant starch: Cook/cool/reheat rice/potatoes for extra resistant starch; helps gut health.
- Collagen/gelatin-rich options if tolerated: Bone broth, slow-cooked meats; pair with vitamin C source for collagen synthesis.

Foods/approaches to limit
- Ultra-processed foods, refined sugars, white flour snacks, fried fast foods.
- High omega-6 industrial oils in packaged foods (corn, soybean, cottonseed) — prioritize olive/avocado oil.
- Excess alcohol (≤3–4 drinks/week, none on flare/flow days if symptoms worsen).
- If suspected triggers: trial 2–4 weeks of reducing lactose, highly processed gluten, and alcohol; reintroduce one at a time to assess symptoms. Keep calories adequate.

Cycle- and flare-aware adjustments
- Late luteal and flow days (and during flares 2026-07-10 to 07-13, 2026-08-04 to 08-07):
  - Shift to warm, easy-to-digest meals: soups, stews, congee, dhal, egg-and-rice bowls, oatmeal with seeds/berries.
  - Lower fiber slightly if cramping/bloating; favor cooked veg over raw; reduce crucifers if gassy.
  - Keep protein steady; modestly reduce total carbs if activity drops, but include easy carbs around sessions (25–40 g).
  - Hydration with electrolytes; ginger or peppermint tea for nausea/bloating.
- Follicular to mid-cycle (post-flow to ovulation):
  - Higher training loads: modestly increase carbs (0.5–1.0 g/kg/day more), keep fats moderate.
  - Emphasize iron-rich foods post-period: grass-fed red meat 1–2x/week, mussels/clams, legumes, spinach with vitamin C.
- Luteal (pre-flow):
  - Appetite may rise: front-load protein and fiber; plan snacks to prevent cravings.
  - Emphasize magnesium- and potassium-rich foods (pumpkin seeds, dark greens, bananas, potatoes, yogurt) for cramps/bloating.

Pre/post-workout nutrition
- 60–120 min pre: Balanced meal with 0.5–1 g/kg carbs + 25–35 g protein + some fats if >90 min before. Example: quinoa bowl with salmon, greens, olive oil.
- 30–60 min pre (if needed): Light carb snack 20–30 g (banana + 1 tbsp almond butter, or oat bar) and water.
- Within 60 min post: 25–35 g protein + 0.5–0.8 g/kg carbs, especially on strength/tempo days. Example: Greek yogurt with berries and honey + rice cakes; or tofu stir-fry with rice.
- On deload/flare days: Keep protein consistent; scale carbs to hunger/activity; sip broths or smoothies if appetite is low.

Micronutrient focus
- Omega-3 EPA/DHA: If fish <2x/week, consider algae oil or fish oil per clinician guidance.
- Magnesium: Food-first (pumpkin seeds, almonds, legumes, greens, dark chocolate). Supplement only with clinician approval, especially around luteal/flow for cramps and sleep.
- Iron: Monitor if heavy periods; pair iron-rich foods with vitamin C; avoid tea/coffee within 60 min of iron-rich meals for better absorption.
- Vitamin D: Check status with clinician; supplement if deficient.
- Calcium: 1000 mg/day from dairy/fortified alternatives, greens, tofu set with calcium.
- Polyphenols: Green tea, hibiscus, turmeric/black pepper, berries daily.

Sample 1-day menus
- Training day
  - Breakfast: Steel-cut oats cooked with chia/flax; blueberries; Greek yogurt; drizzle of olive oil; green tea.
  - Lunch: Salmon, quinoa, roasted carrots/broccoli, arugula-olive oil-lemon salad; kefir or kombucha if tolerated.
  - Snack: Apple + walnuts; turmeric-ginger tea.
  - Dinner: Turkey and veg chili (beans, tomatoes, peppers, onions) over brown rice; side of avocado.
  - Dessert: 1–2 squares 85% dark chocolate.
- Flare/flow day (gentle, soothing)
  - Breakfast: Warm oatmeal with banana, cinnamon, peanut butter; ginger tea.
  - Lunch: Lentil-dhal with basmati rice; sautéed spinach; yogurt or coconut yogurt.
  - Snack: Smoothie (pea/whey protein, mixed berries, spinach, flax, almond milk).
  - Dinner: Chicken-rice soup with carrots/celery; olive-oil drizzle; sourdough; peppermint tea.

Habit and prep system
- Batch-cook 2 proteins (e.g., salmon, turkey), 2 carbs (rice, potatoes), 3 veg (roasted tray), 1 sauce (tahini-lemon) on Sundays.
- Keep a “fast anti-inflammatory snack kit”: nuts/seeds mix, fruit, protein yogurt, hummus + carrots, sardines + whole-grain crackers.
- Spice rack: premix turmeric-ginger-cinnamon-black pepper for easy use.
- Aim for 80–90% whole-food adherence; allow 10–20% flexible foods to sustain consistency.

Body composition or scale goals
- If fat loss desired: modest 250–350 kcal/day deficit via portion control (start by reducing added fats by 1–2 tsp/meal and starch by 1/4–1/2 cup at dinner). Keep protein high; do not push deficits during flares or days with low appetite/pain.
- If maintenance/performance: fuel training days at higher end of carb range; keep recovery snacks consistent.

GI comfort tips
- Chew thoroughly, eat slowly, smaller frequent meals if bloated.
- Favor cooked over raw veg during flare/flow.
- Trial removing high FODMAP foods only if recurring GI distress, ideally with a dietitian.

Supplements (only with clinician approval)
- Omega-3 (EPA/DHA 1–2 g/day combined) if fish intake is low.
- Magnesium glycinate 200–400 mg at night for cramps/sleep if not contraindicated.
- Curcumin 500–1000 mg with piperine, taken with meals, if tolerated.
- Vitamin D per labs; iron only if indicated by labs.

Tracking and adjustments
- Rate daily symptoms (pain, bloating, energy, cravings) 1–10.
- If pain/flare increases, simplify to warm, soft foods, maintain protein, reduce roughage, and prioritize hydration/electrolytes.
- If training quality drops for 3+ sessions, increase carbs by 0.5 g/kg/day for a week and reassess.

This plan complements the training phases, supports recovery, and flexes with her cycle and flares while keeping meals practical and enjoyable.

- Zone 2 (easy/aerobic base): RPE 4–5, conversational, 60–75% max HR.

- Optional MAF cap: keep HR ≤ 180 − age (~146 bpm) for Zone 2.

- 2–3 Zone 2 sessions/wk, building from 30 min to 45–60 min.
- 1 tempo session/wk starting Week 3 (skip or swap to Zone 2 during flow/flare weeks).
- Optional easy recovery walk 20–30 min on rest days.
- Modality mix: incline walk, bike, rower, swim; choose bike/elliptical on high-lift days to reduce impact/fatigue.

- Warm-up each cardio session: 5–8 min easy ramp + 2–3 mobility drills (ankle rocks, hip openers, T-spine).
- Cool-down: 3–5 min easy + 2–3 min diaphragmatic breathing.

  - Z2-A: 30 min easy walk/bike (RPE 4–5). If on flow, keep to gentle walk/bike.

  - Z2-A: 35 min easy.
  - Z2-B: 35–40 min easy.
  - Optional: 20–25 min recovery walk or easy swim.

Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Extend duration, introduce steady tempo; adjust around flare 07-10 to 07-13 and period ~07-24 to 07-27
- Week 5 (06-29 to 07-05) — early-week flow taper then resume
  - Z2-A: 35–40 min easy (during/just post-flow).
  - Z2-B: 45 min easy.

Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Consolidate base, peak steady-state; flare 08-04 to 08-07

  - Z2-A: 50 min easy (try outdoor walk with hills or steady bike).
  - Tempo: 2 x 12 min at RPE 6.5–7, 3 min easy.
  - Optional Z2-B: 30–35 min easy or easy swim.

  - Early week:
    - Z2-A: 45–50 min easy on 08-03.
  - During flare: 25–35 min gentle Z2 only; no tempo.
  - Weekend: 35–40 min Z2 as feels good.
- Week 11 (08-10 to 08-16)
  - Z2-A: 50–55 min easy.
  - Tempo: 3 x 8–10 min at RPE 6.5–7, 3 min easy.
  - Optional Z2-B: 30–35 min easy walk/bike.
- Week 12 (08-17 to 08-23)
  - Z2 long: 55–60 min easy (cap HR at MAF).
  - Tempo: 20 min continuous at RPE ~6.5 if symptom-free; otherwise split to 2 x 10 min or make it Z2.
  - Optional: 20–30 min recovery walk.

Scheduling with strength
- Place the longest Z2 on a non-leg day or rest day.
- Put tempo 6–24 hours away from heavy lower-body sessions (e.g., Day C or a separate day). If same day, lift first, tempo later and shorter.
- During flow/flare, pair Z2 with mobility/breathing sessions and reduce total weekly minutes by ~20–30% if fatigue or pain rises.

Modalities and setups
- Incline treadmill walk: 4–8% incline at brisk pace for Z2 without impact.
- Stationary bike: Upright or spin bike for both Z2 and tempo; cadence 80–95 RPM.
- Elliptical: Good for low pelvic impact; monitor RPE.
- Rowing: Great full-body—use comfortably; back off if pelvic/abdominal pressure.
- Swimming/aqua-jog: Excellent during flares if comfortable.

Optional aerobic benchmarks
- Talk test: Maintain full-sentence conversation in Z2.
- Field test (Week 3 and Week 11): 30-min Z2 steady effort—record average HR/pace and RPE to track improved pace at same HR.
- Step count goal: 7.5k–10k most days; maintain on flare/flow with gentle walks.

Autoregulation
- If next-day leg soreness or pelvic discomfort >3/10, cut tempo volume by 25–50% that week and keep Z2 only.
- If sleep <6 hours or elevated stress, cap sessions at 30–35 min Z2.

This add-on builds a robust aerobic base while honoring her symptom windows and the no-HIIT/no-jumping/no-Valsalva constraints.

- Keeps bracing gentle (brace-and-blow), avoids breath-holding and peak intrapelvic pressure.
- Provides clear numbers for future programming (e1RMs, rep PRs, power distances).
- Lower injury risk and less fatigue so recovery into the next block is smoother.

  - Day B Upper+Core (RPE 7–8): DB bench top set 6 @ RPE 8 + 2x6 @ RPE 7–7.5. Chest-supported row 4x8 @ RPE 7.5. Half-kneeling landmine press 3x6–8 @ RPE 7.5. Wide pulldown 3x8 @ RPE 7. Core triset (60s rest): Pallof 3x10/side + side plank 3x30s + dead bug 3x6/side.
  - Day D Full-Body (RPE 7–8): Trap bar DL 4x4 @ RPE 7.5–8; Bulgarian split squat 3x6–8/side; push-up tempo 3-0-1 3x8–12; seated cable row 3x8–10; hip thrust iso hold 2x20–30s.

  - Z2-A: 35–40 min.
  - Z2-B: 45 min.
  - Tempo: 3 x 7–8 min @ RPE 6.5–7 (3 min easy).
- HIIT-lite (allowed): Air bike 30/90 build 8–9 rounds.
- Plyometrics (allowed, separate by 48h from heavy lower)
  - Broad jump submax to stick 5x3; pogo + line-hop combo 3 sets (8 pogos + 6 line hops); box jump up 16–18” 4x3; med-ball overhead throw 3x6. ~70 contacts.

Week 6 (07-06 to 07-12) — Flare 07-10 to 07-13; front-load intensity 07-06 to 07-09
- Strength (early week push)
  - Day A Lower: Squat 5x4 @ RPE 7.5–8; RDL 4x5–6 @ RPE 7.5; reverse lunge 3x8/side; calf raise 3x15.
  - Day B Upper: DB bench 5x5 @ RPE 7.5–8; 1-arm row 4x8 @ RPE 7.5; overhead press 4x5–6 @ RPE 7.5; face pull 3x12; Pallof 3x10/side.
- During flare (07-10 to 07-13): LISS + light circuits 2 rounds RPE 5–6 only; no tempo, no plyo, no HIIT.
- Conditioning/aerobic
  - Early week: Z2-A 45 min; Tempo 2 x 10–12 min @ RPE 6.5–7 (3 min easy).
  - Flare days: 25–35 min gentle Z2 on 1–2 days max.
- HIIT-lite (allowed early week only): Cruise surge 4–5 x 2 min @ RPE 7.5–8 with 2–3 min easy (do before 07-10).
- Plyometrics (allowed early week only): Rebound ankle hops low 3x12; skater hop short 4x3/side; hurdle step-over to mini-hop 3x5/side; med-ball chest pass 3x8 (~60 contacts). Suspend during 07-10 to 07-13.

Week 7 (07-13 to 07-19) — Post-flare rebuild to moderate-high, not full deload
- Strength (RPE 7–7.5, restore volume)
  - Day A Lower: Front squat 4x4–5; RDL 4x6; split squat 3x8/side; hip thrust 3x6–8.
  - Day B Upper: DB bench 4x6; chest-supported row 4x8; landmine press 3x6–8; pulldown 3x8–10; side plank reaches 3x25–30s; Pallof rotation 2x10/side.
  - Day D Full-Body: Trap bar DL 4x3–4; step-up 3x8/side; push-up 3x8–12; cable row 3x8–10; hip thrust 3x8.
- Conditioning/aerobic
  - Z2-A: 40–45 min.
  - Z2-B: 30–35 min.
  - Optional tempo: 2 x 8 min @ RPE 6.5 only if fully recovered; otherwise Z2.
- HIIT-lite: Skip this week.
- Plyometrics: Optional reduced volume: box jump 12–16” 3x3; low pogos 2x10; lateral line hops 2x10; med-ball scoop 2x6/side (~40–45 contacts).

Week 8 (07-20 to 07-26) — Period expected ~07-24 to 07-27; push early-week, taper during flow
- Strength
  - Day A Lower (pre-flow): Squat top set 4 @ RPE 8, then 3x4 @ RPE 7.5; RDL 4x5 @ RPE 7.5; reverse lunge 3x8/side; hip thrust 3x6–8 (1s pause).
  - Day B Upper (pre-flow): DB bench top set 5 @ RPE 8 + 3x5 @ RPE 7.5; 1-arm row 4x8; overhead press 3x5–6; face pull 3x12; Pallof-to-overhead 3x8/side; side plank 3x30–35s.
  - Day C/D during flow: light full-body circuit 2–3 rounds RPE 5–6: box squat 12; dowel hinge 12; incline push-up 10; band row 12; glute bridge 12; dead bug 6/side.
- Conditioning/aerobic
  - Pre-flow: Z2-A 45–50 min; Tempo 3 x 8–10 min @ RPE 6.5–7 (3 min easy).
  - During flow: Z2 30–35 min; no tempo.
- HIIT-lite: Do early week only if symptom-free; otherwise skip.
- Plyometrics: Early week only if fully symptom-free: broad jump 3x3; pogos 3x10; skater step-to-hop 3x3/side; med-ball chest pass 3x8 (~50–55 contacts). Skip during flow.

Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Consolidate strength, aerobic peak, controlled power; deload for flare Week 10; safe testing in Week 12

Week 9 (07-27 to 08-02) — Post-flow; resume progressive work
- Strength
  - Day A Lower: Front or goblet squat 4x5 @ RPE 7–8; RDL 4x6; step-downs 3x6/side (3s eccentric); hip thrust 3x6–8 (heavier).
  - Day B Upper+Core: DB bench 4x5–6; 1-arm row 4x8; landmine press 3x6–8; wide pulldown 3x8; Pallof press to overhead raise 2x10/side; side plank 3x30s.
  - Day D Full-Body: Trap bar DL 4x3–4 @ RPE 7–8; Bulgarian split squat 3x6/side; push-up 3x8–10; seated cable row 3x8–10; hip airplane holds 2x20s/side.
- Conditioning/aerobic
  - Z2-A: 50 min easy.
  - Tempo: 2 x 12 min @ RPE 6.5–7 (3 min easy).
  - Optional Z2-B: 30–35 min easy or easy swim.
- HIIT-lite (allowed): Cruise surge 6 x 2 min @ RPE 7.5–8, 2–3 min easy.
- Plyometrics (allowed): Box jump 16–20” 5x3; pogo+line-hop combo 3x16 contacts; lateral bound to stick 4x3/side; med-ball rotational scoop 3x6/side (~75–80 contacts).

Week 10 (08-03 to 08-09) — Flare 08-04 to 08-07; deload/flare-friendly
- Strength
  - Early week (08-03) technique session RPE6: Squat 3x6; DB RDL 3x8; reverse lunge 2x8/side; DB bench 3x8; row 3x10; Pallof 2x12/side.
  - During flare: switch to mobility + breathing + very light circuit as tolerated (RPE 5–6).
  - Weekend: Light full-body circuit 2–3 rounds as in Week 8 flow template.
- Conditioning/aerobic
  - Early week: Z2-A 45–50 min.
  - During flare: 25–35 min gentle Z2; no tempo.
- HIIT-lite: None.
- Plyometrics: None.

Week 11 (08-10 to 08-16)
- Strength (RPE 7–8)
  - Day A Lower: Front or back squat 4x4–5; RDL 4x5–6; step-up 3x8/side; hip thrust 3x6–8; band abduction 2x15.
  - Day B Upper+Core: DB bench 4x5–6; 1-arm row 4x8; overhead press 3x5–6; pulldown 3x8; Pallof 3x10/side; side plank 3x30–35s.
  - Day D Full-Body: Trap bar DL 4x3–4; Bulgarian split squat 3x6/side; push-up 3x8–12; seated cable row 3x8–10; hip thrust 3x6–8; bird dog 3x6/side.
- Conditioning/aerobic
  - Z2-A: 50–55 min.
  - Tempo: 3 x 8–10 min @ RPE 6.5–7 (3 min easy).
  - Optional Z2-B: 30–35 min easy.
- HIIT-lite (allowed): Air bike 30/90 build 9–10 rounds.
- Plyometrics (allowed): Broad jump clusters (2+1) x3; continuous low pogos 3x15; lateral line hops 3x16; med-ball overhead throw 3x6 (~80 contacts).

Week 12 (08-17 to 08-23) — Testing and peak quality; no true 1RM
- Strength testing (submax with e1RM)
  - Choose 1–2 primaries (squat, trap bar DL, DB bench/barbell bench if used). Warm up to:
    - Option A: Top set of 3 @ RPE 8 (≈2 RIR), or
    - Option B: Top set of 5 @ RPE 8.
    - Estimate 1RM: Epley = load × (1 + reps/30). Do 1–2 back-off sets at −8–10%.
  - Single-leg index: Bulgarian split squat 6RM/side @ RPE 8; target <10% side gap.
  - Power checks: Med-ball chest pass or scoop toss (2–4 kg), best of 3–5; tempo push-ups max quality reps in 60s at 3-0-1.
  - Strength endurance: Hip thrust max reps at ~60% of typical 6RM (cap 20 reps).
  - Keep anti-Valsalva; stop any test if pelvic pressure/pain increases.
- Non-testing lifts (if time): Keep RPE 6–7, low volume.
- Conditioning/aerobic
  - Z2 long: 55–60 min easy (cap HR at MAF).
  - Tempo: 20 min continuous @ RPE ~6.5 if symptom-free; otherwise 2 x 10 min or Z2.
- HIIT-lite (allowed): One session favorite protocol, cap RPE 8–8.5, shorter volume.
- Plyometrics (allowed): Box jump 18–20” 4x3; pogo + mini forward hops 3x14; skater hop 4x4/side; med-ball chest pass 3x8 (~75 contacts). Skip if any symptom uptick.
- Post-testing micro-deload suggestion (Week 13): Z2, mobility, technique RPE 5–6.

HIIT-lite session menu (only on non-flow, non-flare weeks; 1/week)
- Air bike 30/90 build: 6–10 rounds of 30s hard (RPE 8–8.5) / 90s easy.
- Bike cruise surges: 5–6 x 2 min @ RPE 7.5–8 / 2–3 min easy.
- Elliptical ramps: 8–10 x 40s @ RPE 8 / 80s easy.
- Pool strides: 10 x 30s @ RPE 8 / 60–90s easy.
- Safety: low-impact modalities, exhale through effort, long recoveries. Replace with Z2 on yellow/red-flag days.

Plyometric progression (non-flow, non-flare; 1/week, 48h away from heavy lower)
- Week 2: snap-downs, low pogos, broad jump to stick, lateral line hops, MB chest pass (~60 contacts).
- Week 3: box jump up 12–16” 4x3, pogos 3x12, skater step-to-hop 4x3/side, MB scoop toss 3x6/side (~60–70).
- Week 5: broad jump 5x3, pogo+line-hop combo 3 sets, box jump 16–18” 4x3, MB overhead 3x6 (~70).
- Week 6 (before 07-10): low ankle rebounds 3x12, short skaters 4x3/side, hurdle step-over → mini-hop 3x5/side, MB chest pass 3x8 (~60). Skip during flare.
- Week 7 (optional reduced): box jump 3x3, pogos 2x10, lateral line hops 2x10, MB scoop 2x6/side (~40–45).
- Week 8 (early week only if symptom-free): broad jump 3x3, pogos 3x10, skater step-to-hop 3x3/side, MB chest pass 3x8 (~50–55). Skip during flow.
- Week 9: box jump 16–20” 5x3, pogo+line-hop 3x16, lateral bound to stick 4x3/side, MB rotational 3x6/side (~75–80).
- Week 11: broad jump clusters (2+1) x3, continuous pogos 3x15, lateral line hops 3x16, MB overhead 3x6 (~80).
- Week 12: box jump 18–20” 4x3, pogo + mini forward hops 3x14, skater hop 4x4/side, MB chest pass 3x8 (~75). Skip on any symptom uptick.

Weekly scheduling template (adjust around flow/flare)
- Mon: Day A Lower + optional short Z2 (20–30 min) later.
- Tue: Plyo (if allowed) + Upper OR Upper then plyo first in session.
- Wed: Z2 long (45–55 min).
- Thu: Conditioning day: Tempo or HIIT-lite if allowed; otherwise Z2.
- Fri: Day D Full-Body strength.
- Sat: Optional Z2 30–40 min or easy swim.
- Sun: Rest and mobility.
- During flow/flare: front-load heavier days, then switch to Z2 + light circuits only; skip plyo/HIIT.

Autoregulation and substitutions
- Green light: pain ≤2/10 during/after, no next-day increase—proceed.
- Yellow: pain 3–5/10 or notable fatigue—reduce load 10–20%, cut 1 set, choose unilateral/stability options, keep Z2 only.
- Red: pain >5/10, cramping, pelvic pressure—stop strength/plyo/HIIT; do breathing, mobility, gentle Z2 or rest.
- Substitutions: swap squat for box/goblet/hack; hinge for KB deadlift/pull-through; lunges for step-ups or single-leg press; choose bike/elliptical/swim over running.

Fueling and recovery guardrails
- Heavy or tempo/HIIT-lite days: carbs toward higher end (4–5 g/kg/day), fluids + electrolytes; post-session 25–35 g protein + 30–60 g carbs.
- Late luteal/flow/flare: warm, cooked meals; slightly lower fiber; steady protein; ginger/peppermint tea; hydrate well.
- Sleep 7.5–9 h; 10–15 min evening mobility/breathing on push weeks.

Testing guidance (Week 12)
- Prefer submax e1RM via top set 3–5 @ RPE 8. No true 1RM due to pelvic-floor/valsava risks.
- If a heavy single is desired, cap at ~90% (RPE 8–8.5), one lift only, with spotters/safeties, strict no-breath-holding, and abort at any symptom signal.

This comprehensive plan integrates strength, aerobic base, HIIT-lite, and gentle plyometrics while honoring her endometriosis-related constraints and cycle. It provides progression, deloads around symptom windows, and a safe testing finish to inform the next block.

All flow and flare days strictly exclude HIIT and jumping, and avoid heavy Valsalva throughout.

Key dates and rules
- No HIIT, no jumping, no heavy Valsalva on flow days and during flares.
- Last period 2026-05-04; average 27 days, 4 flow days. Expected periods during plan:
  - ~2026-05-31 to 06-03 (overlaps Week 1)
  - ~2026-06-27 to 06-30 (Week 4–5 boundary; treat early Week 5 as post-flow)
  - ~2026-07-24 to 07-27 (Week 8–9 boundary; treat early Week 9 as post-flow)
- Flares: 2026-07-10 to 07-13 (Week 6–7) and 2026-08-04 to 08-07 (Week 10).
- Global weekly structure (flex around symptoms):
  - 4 lifting sessions (Lower, Upper+Core, Conditioning/Tempo/HIIT-lite, Full-Body) + 2–3 aerobic sessions (Z2, tempo, HIIT-lite) + 1 plyo where permitted + 2 rest days.
  - On flow/flare: lifting becomes light circuits (RPE 5–6), cardio becomes Zone 2 only, and plyo/HIIT omitted.

Intensity and cueing
- Use RPE 1–10. Default RPE 6–8 except deload/flare weeks.
- No heavy Valsalva. Cue: inhale on lower, long exhale through effort (“brace and blow”). Stop with pelvic pressure, cramping >3/10, or pain spikes.

Warm-up (every session, 8–12 min)
- 3–5 min easy cardio
- Mobility: cat-cow, 90/90 hip switches, ankle rocks, open books (1–2x6–8)
- Activation: glute bridges, band lateral walks, dead bugs, band pull-aparts (1–2x8–12)
- Landing prep on plyo days: snap-downs 2x6; altitude drop 2x5 (6–8”)

Cool-down (5–8 min)
- 2–3 min easy spin/walk + hip/hamstring/adductor/T-spine stretches + 2–3 min diaphragmatic breathing.

Core and pelvic-floor-friendly choices
- Favor dead bug, bird dog, side plank, Pallof press/rotation, glute bridge march.
- Regress bilateral to unilateral, shorten ROM, or switch to relief positions if symptoms rise.

Nutrition (anti-inflammatory, daily anchors)
- Protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day; carbs 3–5 g/kg/day baseline (higher on heavy/tempo/HIIT-lite days); fats 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day from EVOO, nuts, seeds, fatty fish.
- Fiber 25–35 g/day; 30 plants/week; hydrate 30–35 ml/kg/day (+500–750 ml training days).
- Emphasize fish 2–4x/week, berries/greens, whole grains, legumes, nuts/seeds, fermented foods; limit ultra-processed foods and excess alcohol.
- Cycle-aware meals: warm/easy-to-digest and slightly lower fiber during late luteal/flow and flares; steady protein; ginger/peppermint tea, electrolytes as needed.
- Workout fuel: 20–30 g carbs pre if needed; 25–35 g protein + 30–60 g carbs within 1–2 h post moderate/hard sessions.

Cardio intensity definitions
- Zone 2 (Z2): RPE 4–5, conversational, 60–75% max HR (optional cap ≈ 180 − age = 146 bpm).
- Tempo: RPE 6–7, short phrases talkable.
- HIIT-lite: RPE 8–8.5 surges, long recoveries, low-impact modalities only; never on flow/flare days.

Plyometric rules
- Only when not on flow or flare days. Low amplitude, soft landings, 40–80 contacts/session, work:rest ≥ 1:4. Surface: rubber/turf.

- Red: pain >5/10, cramping, pelvic pressure—stop strength/plyo/HIIT; do breathing, mobility, gentle Z2 or rest.
